notes.title: v3.0.4 - Frost Flower Major Expansion
notes.notes:
Heyyo adventurers, CraftedCircuitry here. I’m finally showcasing and releasing the biggest update to Deep Dark Wrath, v3.0.4 Frost Flower! New areas, new mechanics, stronger enemies, even stronger Enchanted Cards, and more so let’s dive right in!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/4ecef32a6782ebd4fd880e62f3b409909ec659bc.png[/img]

[b]Added:[/b]
[list]
[*] A Frosty New Continuation to the Lore
[*] 3 New Frozen Areas
[*] New Frozen Enemies
[*] New Enchanted Cards
[*] The Flame Dash
[*] New Frozen Mechanics
[*] New Sword Skins and Armor Trims
[*] New Post-Frozen Areas Endgame
[*] Native Linux / SteamOS Port
[*] Linux / SteamOS Port Moving of Save Data from Steam’s Proton Compatibility Layer to Native Downloads Folder Feature (explained below)
[*] As with the Android APK from before being always included, the Linux version is also included in the Installed Files(no matter what OS you use) so the update size of this Expansion will be much bigger than usual.
[/list]
[b]Updated:[/b]
[list]
[*] Cleaned Up Library Entries
[*] Instructions at the Safe Area as the Flame Dash is added
[*] With the help of the Frost, the Full Powered Construct becomes available
[*] Game Manual
[/list]
[b]Fixed:[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed Projectile Spawning of Enemies not stopping even when game is paused
[*] Cutscene Fixes
[*] Fixed Sword Skins and Armor Trims not applying after Loading a Backup
[*] Fixed Generic Controller and Steam Deck compatibility
[*] Revamped all Controller inputs, especially UI Inputs
[*] Frosted Cards Library Entry has glitched Type
[*] Fixed Firebrand Task deactivated even when Firebrand is not active
[*] Fixed Point Change showing on Player when deducting 0
[*] Minor Bugfixing and Further Optimizations
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/10e2006c38337074b4857f33409e615cd60c5b42.png[/img]

[b]Native Linux Support[/b]

Deep Dark Wrath now has a proper Linux build. I mainly did this so the Save Backups are natively accessible so you don’t have to scour through your Proton Compatibility folder. This does also mean the update size is going to be a lot bigger.

With this, the Save Data has been moved. Scroll down near the bottom of this Update article, or read through the Read Me or Official Game Manual accompanied by this Update in the Installed Files to see how moving your Save Data from Proton to Native works.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/2ff59a6c14e6a259f8462cc419d9b5f5b105c410.gif[/img]

[b]The Frost Flower[/b]

After completing the 7 Oracle Cards, a cool breeze fills the entire Dungeon. Opening up the Frozen Areas from the Safe Area and exploring the Construct area lets you see an opening and may answer where the Icicles of the Construct have come from.
Could this area house a power strong enough to conquer the Darkness?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/92f94f8fc8670085adea25eb688962ce7f847752.gif[/img]

[b]The Flame Dash
[/b]
After exploring the new Frozen Areas a bit, you are granted access to the powerful Flame Dash. This allows you to lunge forward in any direction for a price of your Stamina. New Cards like Dash Blast even bolster it further and make it a deadly way to attack!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/1a2aefe8cfd5e12023d459dd2532c3b0d0215869.gif[/img]

[b]New Frozen Areas and Enemies[/b]

Explore 3 new Frozen Areas, an uncharted area of the Ruins, the Frozen Ruins, and the areas near Mount Wintermoon.

The Frozen Areas also hold new Enemies like the Frost Guard and the Ice Spirits. They’re much tankier and have new attacks like the Frost’s own projectile, and the powerful Frost Beam!

[b]New Enchanted Cards[/b]

A ton of new Enchanted Cards become available with the Frozen Areas and Enemies. From Cards that boost your Dash like Dash Blast, boost your Fireball like Waning Frost, or powering up your Oracle options with the mysterious Storm Cards, you now have a ton more options to dive deeper into the Dungeon!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/4aa6b909ba9e791bbed40c109a5a72159862ced6.gif[/img]

[b]The Frost Construct[/b]

With the power of Frost Shards, the Frost Construct becomes fully powered, allowing you to fuse Enchanted Cards you have to your heart’s content. It is no longer limited by Wandering Flames.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/c2fc336b4cb5362ce1fd851e4c0ac18069ca3710.gif[/img]

[b]New Sword Skins and Armor Trims[/b]

Of course, with a new update comes new Sword Skins and Armor Trims! Frost Beam Swords, Icicle Swords, more Scarves, and more are now available for you to try! Summer options like the Straw Hat and the Umbrella Sword are also available!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/64e26f83f5b337f0731f896b1a04517f8728781d.gif[/img]

[b]Optimizations and Bugfixing[/b]

I originally wrote here that the game got a 5 FPS hit in performance, but instead v3.0 Frost Flower actually has good performance improvements to show for.

Due to upgrading to Godot v3.6, not only did some bugs get fixed, Deep Dark Wrath also got a bit more optimized. The lighting was pretty heavy previously and is now fixed, which makes the game run a lot smoother now.

I also fixed a bunch of bugs and compatibility issues with Linux and the Steam Deck. While playable in previous versions, generic controllers and the Steam Deck did not bode well with the UI so that needed to be fixed.

[b]What Could've Been?[/b]

I had one last big idea for after the Frost Flower Expansion, codenamed the Send Off update. You get to fight the Darkness in a proper boss fight, and because of its demise, you get an alternate ending compared to what this v3.0 Expansion will have.

Other things I had in mind were local or online multiplayer mechanics, like Trading with Other Players or a Co-op way to dive the Dungeon. I also had ideas for a true Perma-death challenge where the Save you have(since you only have one) will have its progress erased when the Adventurer fails the Dungeon.

These were ideas I had written down way back then. But as much as these sounded cool back then, these won’t be added to Deep Dark Wrath.

[b]Final Send-off[/b]

I will still update this game with bug fixes if any glitches or bugs arise or optimizations if there are any new things I can find. But at the end of it, this is the end for me and Deep Dark Wrath. It’s been a wild learning experience and I hope to bring all of these new insights into the future games I make. I will still be avidly playing this on travels or when I’m a bit bored and just want to play a nice slightly challenging game.

This has been a dream in the making, and while I’ve had some tough times with it, it’s been a wonderful and enjoyable experience to finally make this game a reality. Thank you, all of you, for the support!

I post regularly on my Tumblr on projects I do so if you'd like you can stay tuned there!. But for the most part, this has been CraftedCircuitry, signing off for now. Until next time!  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/5d4ff46281902ba658a1eb8d1a320902741baf2c.png[/img]

[b]For Linux and Steam Deck users:[/b]

To seamlessly move your save file from the previous v2.9.9 version under the Proton layer to the Native Linux Backup:

[olist]
[*] Boot up Deep Dark Wrath. Don’t be alarmed that there is no save file yet.
[*] Make sure to not move too much and stay in the Square underneath the Deep Dark Wrath logo.
[*] Press and Hold the Standard Attack Button [ LMB / J / Triangle on PS / Y on Xbox ].
[*] After holding it, you will be prompted to continue holding to move the save to the Native Downloads Folder. 
[*] Keep holding it to confirm you will be moving your save.
[*] Once the operation is complete, go to the Save Journal at the Campfire, and Load the Backup. Save your Game and now the Save you had before is now successfully moved from the Proton layer to the native.
[/olist]
To save on battery life, running the Deck at 5W TDP and 45-50 FPS Limit can still provide a relatively smooth experience. Turning On Half-Rate Shading also helps battery life with little to no degradation in quality. Tweaking the Manual GPU Clock speed to lower than 1000 can also stabilize the performance better. The absolute limit is 4W TDP and 24 FPS.

notes.title: Steam Deck Compatibility
notes.notes:
[p]Heyyo adventurers! This will be a Quick Info Dump on how Deep Dark Wrath will work on the Steam Deck(as well as SteamOS) users, and certain game mechanics pertaining to Linux, SteamOS, and Steam Deck changes!

[b]From personal testing, the game works fine on the Steam Deck.[/b] I've been playing and testing mostly on the Steam Deck recently. With v3.0+, certain UI navigation fixes were done to properly allow Steam Deck and Generic Controller users to navigate the UI.

[b]Steam Deck Performance Settings[/b]

Focusing on High Quality and Performance
[list]
[*] 8 TDP Limit and Above
[*] 60-70 FPS Limit
[*] Half-Rate Shading Turned OFF
[*] Manual GPU Clock UNSET
[/list]
Focusing on Battery Life (reaches 6-7 hours)
[list]
[*] 5-7 TDP Limit (Lower the Less Battery Consumption)
[*] 45-50 FPS Limit (Lower the Less Battery Consumption)
[*] Half-Rate Shading Turned ON
[*] Manual GPU Clock Set to 1000 and Below
[/list]
Absolute Limit
[list]
[*] 4 TDP Limit
[*] 24 FPS Limit
[*] Half-Rate Shading Turned ON
[*] Manual GPU Clock Set to 1000 and Below
[/list]

[b]Linux, SteamOS, and Steam Deck Folders[/b]

This is basically just the Native Downloads folder of the Linux Distro or the SteamOS Proton Layer. If you use v3.0+, the Native Linux Folder(in the Desktop Mode for Steam Deck and SteamOS) is where the Backups are sent. If you use v2.9.9 and below, the game will use the Proton Layer as there was no Linux version for v2.9.9 and below.
[list]
[*] Previous Proton Main Save Folder - .local/share/Steam/steamapps/compatdata/2891520/pfx/drive_c/users/ste
amuser/AppData/Roaming/CraftedCircuitry
[*] Previous Proton Downloads Folder - .local/share/Steam/steamapps/compatdata/2891520/pfx/drive_c/users/ste
amuser/Downloads
[*] v3.0+ Native Main Save Folder - .local/share/CraftedCircuitry
[*] v3.0+ Native Downloads Folder - ~/Downloads
[/list]

[b]Moving Save from v2.9.9 and Below on Proton to the v3.0+ Native Linux Files[/b]

With v3.0+, the game now has a Native Linux version that uses the Native Directory for placing Files and Save Backups of Deep Dark Wrath.
[olist]

[*] Make sure to not move too much and stay in the Square underneath the Deep Dark Wrath logo.
[*] Press and Hold the Standard Attack Button [ LMB / J / Triangle on PS / Y on Xbox ].
[*] After holding it, you will be prompted to continue holding to move the save to the Native Downloads Folder.
[*] Keep holding it to confirm you will be moving your save.
[*] Once the operation is complete, go to the Save Journal at the Campfire, and Load the Backup. Save your Game and now the Save you had before is now successfully moved from the Proton layer to the native Linux folders.
[/olist]

notes.title: v3.0 Expansion Progress
notes.notes:
Heyyo, CraftedCircuitry here! Gonna quickly dish out some updates on Deep Dark Wrath, and its future expansion update, v3.0!

[b]v3.0? What is it?[/b]

If you haven't read my devlogs before, the idea was to follow the path Monster Hunter games usually do.

Base Game Release > Events > Big Expansion > Events

The final Events part(like v2.0 Depth Challenger) might not happen anymore, but the Big Expansion is something I'm steadfastly building up for. It's looking real nice so far so here's some GIFs of what is to come.

You'll have access to new Moves and new Ways to Attack in this Expansion. Make sure to explore them all once you get to the Expansion after the 7th Oracle Appraisal!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/92f94f8fc8670085adea25eb688962ce7f847752.gif[/img]

Of course, new Enchanted Cards, new Effects, and new Powers will be achievable with the Expansion. An idea I had before was to combine Cards with similar traits(Shadow, Fireballs, etc.) and give them like a Set Bonus when you have enough. Instead, singular Cards you can get do such combination on their own.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/1881a7bdc51bd65a2e9521a14484c82331cfa741.gif[/img]

New Types of Enemies will be coming to the Expansion! Outside of the usual tankier enemies and stronger attacks, new types of attacks will become more apparent and will need you to be ready to take on what's to come!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/1a2aefe8cfd5e12023d459dd2532c3b0d0215869.gif[/img]

[b]Selected for Indie Assemble[/b]

A quick little intermission, Deep Dark Wrath got selected to join the Indie Assemble Sale happening this early May! Still waiting on more details on the sale but if you've been on the fence on Deep Dark Wrath, that's the time you can get it!

[b]Expansion, will there be a Price?[/b]

Unlike MonHun's Bigger Expansions being a separate release or a separate DLC, this is a Free Update. So you can just download it when it releases and you'll be able to get everything in the Expansion!

However, it has been busy. I was hoping to get the update done by the anniversary, 2025 May 27th, but the outside stuff has been pretty hectic. So I'll be pushing the update for June. This should give me more time to let it sit and try it out more, and see if I can polish it as much as I can. This will be the final big update for Deep Dark Wrath, so I do wanna end this with the best I can do.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/345c4a79a5b716c77a544fe4f102be42a57ba1f2.gif[/img]

That's it for now, this has been CraftedCircuitry signing off for now.

notes.title: v2.9.9 - Fury Flower Major Content Update
notes.notes:
Heyyo, CraftedCircuitry again with another update to Deep Dark Wrath! This is a snippet of the v3.0 update(hence the jump from v2.2 to v2.9). So, this will feature some of the mechanics that would be added for v3.0. With this, I may be able to fully complete the v3.0 update in the near future.
I also decided to remake the Safe Area’s music. It’s not the best, but I feel much much better with this compared to the previous Safe Area music so I hope you do give it a listen.

[b]Changelog[/b]

[i]Added[/i]
[list]
[*] Firebrand Task and Furious Tasks
[*] The Mysterious Construct and Fusing of Enchanted Cards
[*] Frosted Enchanted Cards
[*] New Enchanted Cards
[*] Spring-themed Sword Skins and 2 New Sword Skin in a different color
[*] Armor Trims, and 3 Android-exclusive Armor Trims
[/list]
[i]Updated[/i]
[list]
[*] On the Android version, the Touchscreen buttons become more transparent when an Xbox or Playstation controller is used
[*] Background Music for the Safe Area remade
[/list]
[i]Fixed[/i]
[list]
[*] When loading from a Backup, Buttons on Rebinding do not automatically update
[*] Fixed Silent Swings adding more time than the base Wrath Anger timer
[*] Fixed Refresh going over Level 5 due to some Cards giving Refresh Points
[*] Fixed Spawning of a Caves Area Skeleton
[*] Minor Bugfixes
[/list]
[b]Furious Tasks[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/45398e339a8869b6b45379ce6a6a0fd360cd6a0b.gif[/img]

A very recent idea of mine as I was playing Monster Hunter Rise, and discovered its Special License Quests to more easily progress through the story. While on paper, the Oracle Piece rewards the Task gives makes progressing through the game easier, the Furious Tasks are orders of magnitude harder.

Furious Collector and Furious Plunderer forces the Wrath to be angered immediately while Furious Explorer forces you to not be in Point Protection. All 3 needing you to do various collecting and conquering to get the coveted Oracle Pieces as rewards.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/eda5f56ff9f59f33b083ec4451e193306c988a20.gif[/img]

You might also get something special once you’ve completed all 3. Who knows?

[b]Firebrand Task and The Construct[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/8ebf31b4655c7804e72b0c3d9280582dce3652c2.gif[/img]

An augmentation of the idea I had before the Adventurer may be allowed to use The Construct. This task will force you to go through the entire Dungeon finding Wandering Flames in order to open The Construct hidden in the Bewildering Ruins.

The Construct will then allow you to open up interesting choices for your build, allowing you to fuse Permanent, Instant, and Veil Cards into 1 powerful Enchanted Card.

[b]Frosted Enchanted Cards[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/3c56e6a56da99dac0c5c524a3119953d9dbe70ea.gif[/img]

[i](not available in the Safe Area, the GIF is just showcasing what it does)[/i]

Products of fused Enchanted Cards, these are denoted by frosty icons on the Enchanted Card.
They also give out the effect Frost Fortification, which seems to not have any effect on the Adventurer. Maybe the v3.0 Update might shed some light on this effect?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/0cf5ff843c6bfa69c0ea61d3b745eee427685e65.png[/img]

[b]Armor Trims, Sword Skins, and BGM Updates[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/35d324cf87d3d60ed6a33d3480ed567cb4b4a2cb.gif[/img]

A new appearance option in the Options, these are placed on top of the Adventurer giving the Adventurer more options in how they look. Of course, I’m gonna give a lot of options, and PC users can up their options with the included template to make your own!
[list]
[*] Leaf Suit (Spring and Autumn versions)
[*] Floral and Flower (Spring)
[*] Santa Hat (Winter)
[*] And more!
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/ac92edd6aa4d1bafbf2234ec3f08d30301b14eda.gif[/img]

As always, coupling this update are new Sword Skins themed around Spring, plus a few more like the Violet Broadsword! As mentioned, the Background Music for the Safe Area was also remade with the update. It’s a little bit more than 4 chords looped now xD.

[b]Snippets of the Future[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/75b52da2af4a3c560b8150d1224a1f58156e2164.gif[/img]

I didn’t think I had the drive or time to do these updates, but here we are. v3.0 is essentially in sight. It’s still a long way to go though. Frosted Enchanted Cards are a bit more balanced for the content packed into v3.0, so I tried to make fusing of Frosted Cards a little bit more tedious (only 5-7 per Run) with this iteration.

I’m a bit happy with this so far, looking forward to getting more time to do more game development as it has been busier on my end.

That’s all for now. Looking forward to what kind of ideas you make for Card builds with the Frosted Cards, and what kind of designs you try with the Armor Trims, Sword Skins, and Plume Color. This has been CraftedCircuitry, signing off for now.

[b]Changelog[/b]

[b]Cyan Forge[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/dadbdbbb2ba09c374574164262b0305c7d3f0342.gif[/img]

Forge Enchanted Cards with the Cyan Forge. You will need to have at least appraised 1 Oracle Card to unlock this feature in the Safe Area. You will then need 3 of the same Type(Permanent, Veil, Instant) and Level of the Card you want to forge.

This is kind of a pity system as a lot of the Cards before are behind RNG. This will allow you to make most of the Cards you may need. Other Cards that cannot be forged are still behind actually obtaining them, and are usually guaranteed in some fashion anyway.

[b]Winter-themed Cards[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/69d3de4e4a239185d5dcd8f861b47759cf503a59.gif[/img]

The Winter Warmth and Cold Crumble Cards are powerful Veil Cards you can only find in the deepest areas of the Dungeon and only when the Wrath is Angered. They will allow you to tank or pummel your way through enemies respectively. I really wanted to try to make a high-risk, high-reward type of Card with Cold Crumble, and I think I made it.

One other new Veil Card is the Enlightened Flames. This will spawn 4 flames around you, that revolve around you and attack enemies! This can only be forged via the Cyan Forge. I always wanted to add some type of Summoner kind of Card in the game, and this lets you become one. Couple this with Flameboyance, and you’ll be dealing a lot of Fire to the monstrosities in the Dungeon.

These seasonal Enchanted Cards won’t go away, so you can get it whenever you can.

[b]Winter-themed Sword Skins[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/10d86e76c3b54bce8ca268a4e5fc875ce91d0a24.gif[/img]

I’ve added 5 more Sword Skins to the game. No Android exclusives on this one so you can use it from anywhere.
[list]
[*] Frost and Frostbringer(animated) Swords
[*] Icicle
[*] Christmas Tree and Lit Christmas Tree(animated) Swords
[/list]
[b]Small Fixes[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/3aaf9aba8feb31cc6fff9fcfe50734916510ff1f.gif[/img]

I’ve also done some small fixes and optimizations to the game. I removed some mechanics that really weren’t meant to be there and are unused. I’ve also boosted Card Inventory, from 500 to 750. This should give you a lot more space for the new Cards I’ve added these past few months. 

The Tutorial was also revamped to be clearer and more concise. The tutorial updates don't change anything if you've already done that particular tutorial bit once.

[b]Future? (again)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/77c1338ccaca7e78c9a0c8eb40ebc203d25179d4.gif[/img]

That’s really about it for Winter 2024. A lot of this new update is really remixing what Deep Dark Wrath already had and adding a little bit more. I will say this wasn’t what I planned for Winter. However, I really am not ready to take the deep dive into v3.0 and v4.0 yet, so I wanted to just add small bits of the update instead.

Enlightened Flames was actually a v3.0 Card. The Cyan Forge is a derivative of the main mechanic I wanted to add for v3.0, so it’s nice to get some practice for it and so I’ll have a better idea of how to make something similar.

Anyway, hope you all have a great Winter 2024, have fun with the game now that it's on a 35% Off Sale, and have fun getting those new Cards! This has been CraftedCircuitry, signing off for now.

notes.title: v2.0.4 - Depth Challenger Major Content Update
notes.notes:
Heyyo, CraftedCircuitry here! Deep Dark Wrath v2.0.4 brings the biggest update to the game, from the brand new Dried Up Rivers area, gauntlet arenas, new Cards to collect, and some visual updates to better the game. There’s a lot to talk about so let’s go right ahead to what I decided to add.

[b]Changelog[/b]

[i]Added[/i]
[list]
[*] Dried Up Rivers Area
[*] Gauntlet Arenas scattered in the Dungeon
[*] More Currency to Plunder
[*] New Enchanted Cards
[*] More Proper Control Glyphs that update
[*] 2 New Sword Skins, Monochrom and Tidebreaker
[*] Added Keyboard-only UI Helper so you players don’t have to move to Arrow Keys
[/list]
[i]Updated[/i]
[list]
[*] Better Damage
[*] Better Compendium Map
[*] Optimized Enemy Spawning
[*] Quick Access no longer an option and always active
[*] Run Timer more precise and not pausing during Player taking Damage
[/list]
[b]Dried Up Rivers[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/fbc77c4b2c4ce52247be03aa9dca135500d77fd2.gif[/img]

The big new area of Deep Dark Wrath, hidden behind a wall in the Forest and only accessible via a special Challenger Trinket you need to find in the Dungeon. It’s a mid-game/end-game area, featuring some old and some more powerful new enemies as the Wrath corrupts the Rivers near the Forest.

Once you acquire the Challenger Trinket, the Wall blocking it in the Somber Forest will go away when you set the Run Option to open the Dried Up Rivers Area before you start a new Dungeon Run. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/ffd5c0195959c1ce850c972a752dd0ceb9f39d34.gif[/img]

It has the size of roughly 2 Dungeon Areas. It is big and it has a ton of rewards to plunder. Opening the Dried Up Rivers also blocks you from going further to the Caves and beyond, so you have to choose wisely on what you want to do for that Run.

[b]More Enchanted Cards[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/5e058e01e6f03681c85c8c78522415ce8109cef6.gif[/img]

There’s now more Cards, a lot less in Stat-focused and more on Dungeon effects that really breaks the Dungeon wide open. You wanna go full on Mage? You got Desolate Flames to make your Fireballs even more potent. Need better learning of the Dungeon, something like the Revealing Eye may help you.

[list]
[*] Shine Sync - One of the first Cards that actually gives Refresh from the start.
[*] Revealing Eye - A special Veil Card that boosts the efficacy of your Quick Map, not only showing more Interactables but also destroys walls in the Dungeon to make it easier to navigate.
[*] Desolate Flames - A special Veil Card that lets you summon not 1, not 2, but 3 Fireballs in the adjacent directions. You do lose half of their damage though.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/c83109d318d7e0240f2294dae0b89292bdc0f4e5.gif[/img]

And a bunch more! I'd recommend checking out the ‘Enchanted Cards and You’ book in the Compendium to see the new ones and what they do!

[b]Gauntlet Arenas[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/0d5ea138393cd9734380088cd59a1f7640717e92.gif[/img]

Hidden in some parts of the Dungeon are small arenas forcing you to fight a set number of Enemies before you can escape. These will give you some nice Point rewards and some of the new Enchanted Cards.

This was honestly a little bit of a savior feature. With new ideas, means new Enchanted Cards, and where do I put them? Before Gauntlets, I had absolutely no idea. I was thinking I was gonna spam a few in the same area. The Gauntlets gave me new areas to just put them as nice powerful rewards for toughing it out against countless enemies you need to defeat.

The amount of enemies you need is affected by your current amount of Oracle Pieces and the amount you need is mentioned once you enter(and the Wall spawns in to block you in).

[2024-09-13 - Just noticed the GIF for Gauntlet Arenas was not the proper one, so I replaced it with the actual Gauntlets GIF]

[b]New Sword Skins[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/0324ca2bc422ed92f053c2d462f405438cb70336.gif[/img]

A previously Android-only Sword Skin is also available on PC now, the chipped metallic Monochrom Sword. v2.0 also comes with the Philippine flag-inspired Tidebreaker Sword. Let the tides of battle favor you with this colorful sword!

[b]Damage Balancing[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/fdf7499d2be4fd74e6cb7db13d829f7b1e3de008.gif[/img]

To help lessen the need for Damage Cards, I’ve added a 0.1 boost to your base damage for each Card you applied and if you have 2 Cards applied. 

Basically, if you have:
[list]
[*] 1 Card - No Boost
[*] 2 Cards - 0.2 Damage Boost
[*] 3 Cards - 0.3 Damage Boost
[/list]
This does also prompt Damage to be nerfed by 0.3 Damage on each level. What does this mean? Any Damage Card as long as you have 3 Cards active is basically the same, you really won’t feel the change. But just 3 Cards now allows you to have a boost to your damage. While a small boost and not a big boost for lower health enemies, it does help with higher health threats like Brutes, the new Rivers Area enemies, and the Final Area enemies.

[list]
[*] For example, Brutes have 10 health, you would need 10 hits before. With the new change, 3 Cards now only needs 8 hits, allowing for more survivability against spots where enemies surround you very easily and lessens the need for Damage Cards for higher health threats.
[/list]
This still could be balanced further, maybe I’ll further nerf Damage but I think it’s in a good spot for now. As much as I want Enchanted Cards to always be powerful, I also don’t want one to be too polarizing that you *always* need it.

[b]Smaller Updates[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/afeb318f00f063660ed80e47c05ad99a4a6e155b.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] The Compendium’s Map is now made better and uses the updated Quick Map textures so it's actually precise and doesn’t use the old scribbles I made for it back then.
[*] For Keyboard users, you no longer have to switch to the Arrow Keys for UI Controls. You now have the UI Helper(Default is LCTRL) that stops movement when holding the input, and allows for UI navigation and UI Quick Access usage.
[*] For Controller users, inputs have been made far more robust especially when scrolling through the book entries and Inventory.
[*] There are now Control Helper Visuals so you’re not lost in the HUDs and Functions of the Safe Area. That and the Instructions also update to whatever button you rebound that action to.
[*] Quick Access option is always active and is no longer an option
[*] The Stopwatch is now more precise, no longer paused when taking a hit.
[*] Optimizations in Enemy Spawning were also done to further reduce load on your device and further reduce lag.
[/list]
[b]The Future?[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/f3d94032391744faf5b30e0d0c20de7bd16f8340.gif[/img]

I’m gonna quickly talk about my future ideas if I ever get the time and drive to continue this. The game’s experience is based on Monster Hunter, specifically the endgame experience of Iceborne. So there’s a lot of ideas that were derived from playing that franchise. It’s not necessarily a Monster Hunter-like game, but more of evoking the grindy feeling of the endgame experience into a lightweight game. That idea includes how I structure big content updates, Main Game, Main Game’s post-release, Big Expansion, and Big Expansion’s post-release.

[list]
[*] v2.0 features this main post-release update, Depth Challenger. Lots of things that build off of the main game. A more challenging area, new enemies, new Enchanted Cards, and the like.
[*] v3.0, which is the Big Expansion I had in mind, will be much bigger. It’ll have 3 new Areas, a big new mechanic that alters and strengthens your existing Enchanted Cards, a continuation of the lore, and in turn, a new ending. I don’t plan to make this a Paid DLC expansion.
[*] v4.0 simply builds off of the Big Expansion, adds a new encounter and an ending that alters the Big Expansion’s ending.
[/list]
v3.0 and v4.0 are still on paper, and I have no idea if I’ll ever get to it. But it's nice to have some future plans if I ever have the drive to fully complete the ideas outside of the base game. The main idea is already complete, and for now at least, I’m very, very happy with it so far.

[b]That’s About It[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/59e0105dd05d48796e2c59d2e02da10512375d7c.gif[/img]

That’s about it for Deep Dark Wrath. This mid/endgame addition is something I wanted to add to give the end a little more substance other than ‘go for more Oracle Pieces and Points’. The gauntlets also give a little bit more challenge. I’m honestly happy to leave this now if life comes in the way, but I may come back for the 2 Big Content ideas I have eventually.

If you'd like a hint on where the item to unlock Dried Up Rivers is hidden, I'd suggest taking a look at the Ruins area. It’s been fun and again, I hope I can do this again in the near future. This has been CraftedCircuitry, signing off for now. (Hoping for not much bugfixes, I tested and let this update cook for a month)

I really hoped I would have put the newest additions a few weeks from now, but since I only saw the Wrath Anger Fangs visual bug after I was able to do both Quick Map and Oracle Reversion, I kinda needed to put this update out now.

[h3]Quick Changelog[/h3]

[b]Added[/b]
[list]
[*] Oracle Reversion allowing you to modify your Oracle Pieces(in turn modify Dungeon difficulty) once you finish the game
[*] Hold for Quick Area Map via Space / L1 / LT
[*] Another Map HUD at the Front of the Map Table
[*] Icons of Attack(UI Accept) and Regen when they can be used to shortcut for HUDs
[/list]
[b]Fixed[/b]
[list]
[*] Rebinding Options says Dash instead of Sprint
[*] Options Focus Button not losing Focus
[*] Abandon and Abandon-like Buttons still activating even when already hidden
[*] Wrath Bar at a Glance not showing up in subsequent runs after a Wrath Anger
[/list]
[b]V1.1.1 - Some Quick and Easy Updates and Fixes[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/95f82120076381ebd4a503c87ee34d2c746d6e15.gif[/img]

One addition is a Quick Area Map so that you’ll be able to see the map of the area vaguely. The design is very much inspired by Hollow Knight’s own Quick Map.

While I do want Adventurers to gather map knowledge on their own, this will help the onboarding experience a little better so you’re not totally lost. And it only vaguely shows the map, the Points, Enemies, Key Items, and Walls won’t show up. It just shows the rough outline of the area and the entry and exits. Essentially you have the Map in the Compendium in your hands.

Once you have a good idea of what to do, you can just not use it anymore. It’s some option I’ve been thinking about whether I wanted it in or not, but ultimately it’ll help a new Adventurer learn a bit quicker and better. I’m hoping it’ll make for a better experience.

I also had some bugs to fix and some smaller additions added. I also found that the newly added Wrath Anger fangs don’t show up again if you the Wrath got Angered in a previous run. While it is only a visual bug, that’s still an important UI element Adventurers need to see.

[b]V1.1.3 - Oracle Reversion[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/8d2ef6c47ffc6f21a405a37552caca02dd39268d.gif[/img]

This is a weird endgame addition to kind of replay the game without the need to reset saves or reset cards. Yes, it's a way to just reuse and pad content. This was not really part of my post-release plans but was simply a quick idea I had while I rested from Deep Dark Wrath. 

The GIF seems to look like it is skipping some numbers but it does indeed scroll through 0 to 7, and the highest accumulated Oracle Pieces. The highest accumulated amount also accounts for how many you've gained even if you lowered the current Oracle Piece amount.

[b]Just A Few Days after Release[/b]

I’m terribly sorry if the Wrath Fangs visual bug has inconvenienced you. I really should have tested it more and looked into it more. Hoping you all are enjoying the game. This has been CraftedCircuitry signing off for now.

notes.title: V1.0.1 - Full Version Release
notes.notes:
I have finally released my first commercial game, Deep Dark Wrath! Thank you for all the pre-release support, shouting out my friends and family, Feedback Quest 6 Game Jam over on Itch, the various gaming communities on Reddit, and you reading this now. It’s time to engulf this world with a Deep Dark Wrath!

Moving right along, if you have any feedback, please do let me know as I wanna make sure this Full Version is bug-free and performs well for most devices. The game is also on a Launch Sale of 10% Off!

[b]V1.0.1 - The Full Version[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/500c20aa4938904c1cbe33aafc9d68f8d8c54460.gif[/img]

This lightweight grindy game is finally a reality. It’s done, its main idea is complete. 5 Dungeon Areas to get lost in, lots of Enchanted Cards to play around with, the grind experience and feeling I got from endgame MHW:Iceborne, a nice and quick adventure every Dungeon Run, all in a small and lightweight package.

I’ve added some extra little things in the last few weeks to polish the game. To quickly glance at the Wrath’s Anger, you can check the fangs on the top of the screen. Don’t see any? Well, it’s anger isn’t prominent yet. 

There is a small addition to tutorials and info to make things more clear. Point Protection, Old Cards unlocking the Door, and the new At a Glance Bar for Wrath Anger. Onboarding new Adventurers should be much better now.

[b]Future Updates?[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/1c88fbfeb5edc7295274f493b0823eac686833fd.png[/img]

I’ll look into what I can do as I actually have several ideas of how to continue the lore and add more content to the game. I may take a break from Deep Dark Wrath first(after post-release quickfixing if needed)to let my mind be refreshed. It’s also so I could let them sit a little more, and maybe refine them once I start making them.

However, if there are some really good things to help the game like localizing for a specific language that the majority may want, please do leave some feedback down below as it is always appreciated.

You can follow me on my Tumblr for the latest updates on what I’m working on. Maybe in the future, you’ll get a sneak peek of what the future updates are.

[b]Countless Thank Yous[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/59e0105dd05d48796e2c59d2e02da10512375d7c.gif[/img]

Again, I would like to thank you all for the pre-release support. Hoping for a good launch and not many bugfixing. I play this game a good amount once a day, so I know it works well enough. But you never know until you really release it into the wild.

This has been a fun experience. I hope to do this again in the future, and I really do hope you enjoy diving deep in Deep Dark Wrath. This has been CraftedCircuitry, signing off for now.

notes.title: v0.9.17 - Release Date, Hitstop, Stamps, Cloud Saving, and Final Polishing
notes.notes:
Heyyo, it’s CraftedCircuitry again with a small announcement. It’ll only be 2 weeks left until Deep Dark Wrath’s Full release. I'm proud to announce I'm finally nearing its Full Version completion.

[b]As mentioned in the Summary, the release date of Deep Dark Wrath is 2024 May 27, Monday.[/b]

[b]v0.9.10 - Final Bugfixing[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/a9dd6c089a8b3d4539a4ffdbe577ea5e4ab817c3.png[/img]

I still had some time to polish and bugfix and it’s good that I still try to break my game whenever I can. A remnant of an old bug that destroyed a few weeks of game dev was the Area Notifier not properly syncing whether I was in a certain area or not. This time it was in the Hidden Veil Shop, which is a very big misstep if I did not see that bug.

The Area Notifiers have 2 main collision areas, signifying the 2 areas it would connect. What I would do is check collisions to see if the Adventurer has passed through it or not. On my first iterations, it would not properly log what area the Adventurer was in, making it possible where enemies would not spawn in the area you want to go and not properly activating certain important functions for that area.

I fixed it by simply checking if the Adventurer’s current area was already different from the collision’s area, making it more precise.

However, I didn't do it properly for Veil Shop, which resulted in this bug again. This can be easily manipulated by players as there is a very powerful function it does that would essentially break the game if I let the bug happen. Luckily, since I already know how to do it properly, it's an easy fix.

[b]V0.9.11 - Adventurer Hit Effects[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/f0c698e3e7ac64fc0669ad6db8dac1bf96b1e29d.gif[/img]

In pursuit of polishing the game further, I added more hit feeling whenever the Adventurer gets hit. I made it more exaggerated, I emulated the feeling you get on how Hollow Knight does it. Blackening of the screen, shockwaves to see that you got hit, and more red when the Adventurer is already at 1 HP. There’s also a lot more effects when the Adventurer dies in the run. Again, I wanted to add a bit more exaggeration.

I essentially just reused the Oracle Appraisal effect for this so I didn’t really have to make a brand new module. It was also White normally, so I can easily modulate the colors to what I need it to be. It’s the same as the small effects you get when Enchanted Cards apply, the Adventurer healing, or when they get Points. The effect only ever gets used for the Oracle so I might as well reuse it.

[b]V0.9.12 - Stamps[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/7e9790e5d4eba0d4ab421f6a1b75a9eff4d4f5f4.png[/img]

The Adventurer can now get Stamps from their adventures that automatically show up in their Save Journal. This is only saved on your Save Data and is not connected to stuff like Steam’s Achievements system. I might add the functionality post-release.

I’ve even added a little Info page in the Dungeon Chronicles so you can get a hint of how to get the three Stamps on your Save Journal.

[b]V0.9.17 - Plume Color[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/dc65e79d4795c6750d909bc73b83d738c6a65fd1.gif[/img]

Something that’s been on the backburner for a long time, didn’t even write it on my to-do lists and documents. A small little change that lets Adventurers change their Plume Colors. It adds some nice more personality in your adventures as your venture deep into this deep Dungeon.

The simple color bar was changed to the sprite of the Adventurer eventually as it’ll help you get a glimpse of what it looks like without having to go out of the Options Menu.

[b]Overestimated Requirements[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/757f19232cd02138e523962073507cfbb892913e.png[/img]

I sadly over-estimated the minimum requirements for a PC. I had only been testing the demo on the lowest spec laptop I have available and it can run it, for a lack of a better way to say it. I only tested the Full Game recently, and well, it doesn’t run xD. I really thought GLES2 could save me with lower budget spec hardware, but with how I made the game, it was just not able to. GLES2 still saves me on older Androids which is still very good though.

I’m just gonna play it safe and put the recommended requirements as the minimum. At the very least it actually runs properly and very smoothly. Going lower will still be fine if ever anyone wants to try, but the lower the spec you go, the less performance and less guarantee it actually runs.

[b]Ready for Cloud Saving[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/946f3c2877f417e0f9ad5f992fec8067d8a4f0a2.png[/img]

Yes, I was honestly debating whether to add this or not. But it always stuck in my mind that this is a grindy game. Adding Cloud Save to Steam is another layer of protection with the Save Backup functionality of the Save Journal. I decided to do it, it was pretty easy with Steam's Auto-Cloud anyway, and I got it working in literal minutes.

I’ve done some developer tests and it seems to be working flawlessly. What’s nice is that both this and the Save Journal Backing Up work very seamlessly together.

[b]A Quick Ending to a Quick Announcement[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/1f63f9c8b09f9a8c3d1b9fdc13c4fe1d2d5aef1f.gif[/img]

I feel like a broken record, but it’s simply just polishing and playtesting as the game is about to release in roughly 2 weeks. Hoping for a good launch, and once again, thank you for all the support.

This has been CraftedCircuitry, signing off for now.

notes.notes:
I rested a lot during these past few weeks so updates have been really slow. Now that I am a bit more rested, I am a bit more ready for the coming weeks until Deep Dark Wrath’s Full Version release. There’s a bigger focus on polishing and finalizing the game so the changes aren’t going to be too big.

[h3]v0.9.7 - Flameboyance[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/bdc88bb90ab7b11edecc244535b17cfe5446baf6.png[/img]

I was planning on putting Flameboyance into a future Post-release update, but I decided to add it here now if I ever take a long time to add the Post-release content updates of this game. I want to make this game complete out of the box, and having more options to venture the Dungeon helps that.

[h3]v0.9.8 - More Bugfixing[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/90da503168dbb000a25ffe55625b9dd20c177e74.png[/img]

While testing some features out, I noticed that the Config was not loading properly from the Backup. I kept trying and trying and somehow it just did not work. I looked through the code and kept trying to find the culprit, and it was a simple variable I did not change. 

Loading player progress uses a single Load Static function, and in that function it needs a variable of whether it’ll load from the actual save data or from the backup save data. At the very end, the config loading is supposed to be loaded. It actually takes in the same variable.

The problem? The config loading was always set to False, meaning it would always attempt to load from the actual save data and not backup. This works fine normally but if I want to load from backup, well it did not work. That was a bit of a headache xD but I finally fixed it.

I actually had a bug that I did not mind with the Fireball. I added lights to it before, but didn’t make it more apparent. Some feedback on Reddit gave me a reason to revisit it, and apparently the lights did not properly follow the direction of the Fireball. It’s now fixed and the lights made more apparent, which adds a lot more life to that attack.

I’ve also been doing my final tweaks to the game, upping Sound Effects and Background Music and the like.

[h3]Updates to the Compendium[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/fe97f1b0514df7cac53d2d506c5785482d7a06c9.png[/img]

I added more clarifications, re-iterated some more information, and added information about the recent additions like the Flameboyance Card and the Special Points. I’ve been looking to also be more mindful of the grammar in the Books and rewriting when necessary.

[h3]Visual Updates[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/71a93e8dff586fef2f5d32ceab97e7de4e60bcfc.png[/img]

Lots of updates recently, so I decided to update the screenshots on the various platforms and the game’s Press Kit to be updated with the recent changes. You can check them out on the game’s various platforms.

The [url=https://www.youtube.com/@CraftedCircuitry/]CraftedCircuitry YouTube[/url] channel is also now filled with tons of Shorts about the various Enchanted Cards you can get. You can check them out if you like.

[h3]Release Date Nearing[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/89566d66b368f0c783d43635fe5080e541a845fc.gif[/img]

I’ll announce the release date 2 weeks before the date. It’s been nice to have some rest from Deep Dark Wrath, playing it with the intention of actually playing it, doing the goals and living the idea of being able to play one of my dream games that have been on my mind for years.

Echoing my previous Devlog’s ending sentiment, thank you all for the support or even just reading through this Devlog. It is much appreciated and it has been fun to show Deep Dark Wrath to the world.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2891520/Deep_Dark_Wrath/

It’s been CraftedCircuitry, signing off for now.

notes.title: v0.8 - The Progress So Far
notes.notes:
[b]Heyyo, I am CraftedCircuitry and welcome to my first to-be-released game, Deep Dark Wrath! It’s been 6 months of game development and it's finally about to be released in a couple of months.[/b]

The game started as an idea when I was playing Monster Hunter World: Iceborne. I wanted to get the endgame grind experience, but at a smaller package. For years the idea of a quick-to-play game was in my head but was left on the backburner because of life. I also haven't really set on a proper idea of what the game loop would be.

But inspiration hit me from a very odd place. I got inspiration from a Minecraft minigame, Decked Out from Hermitcraft. And it finally clicked, I really liked the dungeon diving experience that minigame had so I put a little twist on it and gave it my own flare. 

The game loop for the game was:
[list]
[*] Enter the Dungeon
[*] Gather Points from Dungeon
[*] Safely Escape the Dungeon
[*] Use those Points to buy Enchanted Cards, ideally increasing in rarity and power
[*] Repeat
[/list]
With the end goal of diving deeper and deeper so that you gain more and more Points, access to more powerful Enchanted Cards, and to find the source of the darkness, the Oracle Pieces, at the end of the Dungeon. The Oracle Pieces which can turn into Oracle Cards that can be used to make it easier to dive deeper in the Dungeon, and to hopefully quell the Deep Dark Wrath.

I now had a game loop, a rough idea of what the game will be, and a drive to make this game. It's been 6 months of solo developing and here we are. I'm proud of what I've achieved and done so far. And, I hope people like and enjoy this small game.

[h2]Let me quickly showcase the progress so far.[/h2]

[previewyoutube=iVqy7L14Vyo;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]V0.1[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/27d0089b8a5f0fcc19f16bebfa9c68cb444e823c.png[/img]

Promptly after the idea was finally formulated, I started prototyping the mechanics. Making sure everything works and all that. After weeks of prototyping, I spent almost 2 months completing the content of the game. The vast Dungeon Areas, the challenging Enemies, all the Key Items, and the goal of the game. I already had a pretty good idea of what I want this game to be so it was simply a matter of making the game a reality.

[h2]V0.2[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/65901028495d21bef4fb460333c480f18eef46f1.png[/img]

The Lighting and Feel of the Game were added here. This gave the game the mostly signature look it has now. It's a lot lighter back then as I still wanted to keep the big visibility. This was also when I ripped out the camera movement via mouse as it wasn’t really needed anymore.

[h2]V0.3 - v0.4[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/cb013e8f4e2f5f32e628b763bd65c42cae60c037.gif[/img]

These versions focused on polishing the content and mechanics of the game. This was also the time where I was finally confident enough to start showing off this game to the world and on various social media platforms. 

[h2]V0.5[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/b85ae0942b5a3ae4718258c016c8d9bf08b8755c.gif[/img]

The Fireball was introduced in this progress version, a powerful attack the Adventurer can unlock later down the line(not in the Free Demo). I also did a lot more polishing to this game, of course.

[h2]V0.6 - V0.7[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/5e0aadfda3d728f9bd3a8b436326463732f0d0a7.gif[/img]

The Combat Update happened in v0,6, while a Speed and Pacing Update happened in v0.7. These were 2 very big balancing of mechanics updates that I did due to a lot of feedback from a game jam. These updates helped shaped a better experience for the player as they explore the Dungeon.

I also made this game a bit more optimized for lower-end hardware. It's a fairly simple 2D game, surely it can run on a good range of hardware. A lot more lag was quelled, and a lot of mechanics optimized and made easier to run.

v0.7 is also the version of the Free Demo you can download to try out the game! I’ve been working hard to polish and perfect it, and to give it the best experience so that you get the gist of the game. As such, this is also the point where I finally made and released the Steam Page!

[h2]V0.8[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44933933/11962e34fb2dc5e352d9149c4f7552b262617715.gif[/img]

The Final Stretch of Polishing is here. From little quality of life changes to bug fixes, this current version I’m working on is really about finishing this game. I've still got a lot to do, better sound design, better quality of life changes, and maybe add some Steam Achievements later on.

Multiple times I thought, 'I am done with this game'. I'm glad I didn't just released my game willy-nilly as it wouldn't have been so much better. I'm glad I can introduce this first Steam game to you all, Wishlist the game if you like what you see!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2891520

This has been CraftedCircuitry, signing off for now.
